text: You built an app. People pay for it every month, and it is worth something today.
You just have no way of knowing what.
Every calculator online hands you one number and keeps the reasoning to itself.
Set a price, set a customer count, and you have a first estimate.
You get a valuation, the range around it, and the multiple that produced it.
Then the levers that actually move it: pricing, churn, acquisition.
Move one, and the number moves with it, in front of you.
Every metric is graded against the market: lifetime value over cost, payback, retention, rule of 40.
Where you sit has a name — five tiers, from mice to whales, and each one is a different company to run.
And when you want to know why a number moved, it is written down in plain words.
Or drag a single dove across a plate, and watch a valuation happen under your hand.
No spreadsheet. No sales call. No credit card.
